year: Year 1 (2025-26 core module list, confirmed unchanged since 2023-24)

modules.title: The World Economy: History and Theory
modules.aims: Understanding of global economic development over the past millennium, examining forces explaining regional economic success and obstacles to advancement, emphasising the interaction between rich countries and the rest of the world, and developing research and analytical capabilities.
modules.learningOutcomes: Familiarity with world economic evolution; understanding of economic trends, measurement challenges, and contemporary empirical debates; ability to approach economic problems using modern research methodologies.

modules.title: Macroeconomics 1
modules.aims: To introduce the student to the fundamental determinants of national income, employment, the price level and the foreign balance in the short and long run.
modules.learningOutcomes: Understanding of macroeconomic issues, measurement of aggregates, current policy trends, and capacity to apply theory through structural models using mathematical and graphical techniques.
syllabus: Macroeconomic data: National Accounts, Output, Value Added, GDP, Unemployment, Inflation

modules.title: Microeconomics 1
modules.aims: A thorough grounding in the basic principles of microeconomics, with emphasis on consumer and producer theory application, developing analytical skills across mathematical, graphical, and intuitive approaches to address real-world economic problems.
modules.learningOutcomes: Solid grasp of the basic theoretical material in microeconomics; application to policy analysis and practical scenarios; explanation of concepts using mathematical, graphical and intuitive analysis; understanding of economic model construction and their inherent limitations.
syllabus: Supply and Demand: market equilibrium, elasticities, government intervention
Consumer Theory: preferences, utility, budget constraints, demand, substitution/income effects, revealed preferences, behavioural economics
Production: technology, isoquants, marginal products, cost curves, returns to scale, profit and cost minimisation
Perfect Competition: profit maximisation, market equilibrium, consumer/producer welfare
Imperfect Competition & Game Theory: oligopoly models (Cournot, Stackelberg, Bertrand), collusive equilibria, Nash equilibria

modules.title: Statistical Techniques B
modules.aims: To develop undergraduate students' statistical and computing capabilities for analysing real-world data, gaining exposure to statistical software while learning data description and analysis techniques, providing the quantitative foundation for econometric methods and applied economics.
modules.learningOutcomes: Acquire statistical techniques necessary for first and second year economics modules; develop knowledge of statistical methods and statistical modelling; develop awareness of data handling through statistical software use.
syllabus: Continuous random variables; uniform and normal distributions

modules.title: Mathematical Techniques B
modules.aims: To develop the requisite mathematical and quantitative skills for a rigorous study of contemporary economics, including econometric methods and applied economics.
modules.learningOutcomes: Acquire quantitative tools for first and second year economics modules; develop programming ability in statistical software for graphing and mathematical methods; apply systematic quantitative approaches to economic problems.
syllabus: Calculus of functions of two or more variables
Illustrative applications of all techniques in economics
modules.prerequisiteNote: Strong A-level algebra and calculus knowledge (differentiation and integration rules) assumed.
